title: पठनकला शिक्षण सिकाइको औचित्य Pathankala Shikshan Sikaiko Aauchitya
nepali: लिपिचिह्नद्वारा प्रकट विचारलाई ग्र हण गर्न े  प्रव्रिmया पठन कला हो । ल े ख्य सामग्रीको भनाइ तथा विचारलाई पढेर बुझ् नुु  पठनबोध हो । यसले थोरै समयमा धेरै सामग्री ग्रहण गर्ने क्षमताको विकास गराउँछ । प्रस्तु त अध्ययन पठनबोध शिक्षणको परिचय, उद्देश्य, आवश्यकता र महत्वका साथसाथै पठनको प्रकारमा केन्द्रित छ । यसमा गुणात्मक ढाँचाको अवलम्बन गरी पुस्तकालीय विधिबाट सामग्रीको सङ ् कलन गरी व्याख्या विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । विषयवस्तुलाई आवश्यकताअनुसार दु्रत, मध्यम र मन्द गतिमा पढ ् न, विचार र सार बुझ ् न, व्याख्या विश्लेषण गर्न, टिपोट र प्रश्नोत्तर क्षमतामा अब्बल सावित गराउन पनि पठनबोध महत्वपूर्ण मानिन्छ । पठनबोधलाई सस्वर पठन, मौन पठन र दु्रत पठन गरी छुट ् याएर हेर्न सकिन्छ । विषयवस्तुलाई  आवाज निकालेर अर्को व्यक्ति तथा समूहले सुन्ने गरी पढ ् नु सस्वरपठन हो भने आवाज ननिकाली मनमनै पढ ् ने काम मौनपठनमा गरिन्छ । त्यसैगरी लिपिबद्घ सामग्रीलाई छिटोछिटो पढेर त्यसमा भएको भाव बुझ ् न सक्नु दु्रत पठन हो । पठनबोधका लागि प्रारम्भिक तथा आधारभूत तहमा सस्वर पठन उपयुक्र्त मानिन्छ भने माध्यमिक तथा उच्च तहहरूमा भने मौन पठन र दु्रत पठनको प्रयोग धेरै भएको पाइन्छ । प्रस्तु त लेखले भाषा शिक्षणसँग सम्बन्धित शिक्षक, विद्यार्थी लगायत पाठ ् यक्रम निर्माता तथा पाठ् यपुस्तक लेखकमा सहयोग पु¥याउने  छ ।
american_english:
The process of grasping the ideas revealed through written symbols is the art of reading.
Reading and understanding the statement and the ideas of written material is reading comprehension.
It develops the capacity to grasp a great deal of material in a short time.
The present study is focused on the introduction, objectives, need and importance of teaching reading comprehension, along with the types of reading.
In it, a qualitative design has been adopted, material has been collected through the library method, and explanation and analysis have been carried out.
Reading comprehension is also considered important for making one excel in the ability to read the subject matter at fast, medium and slow speeds as needed, to understand the ideas and the gist, to explain and analyze, and to take notes and answer questions.
Reading comprehension can be looked at by separating it into oral reading, silent reading and rapid reading.
If reading the subject matter aloud so that another person or group may hear it is oral reading, then in silent reading the work of reading silently to oneself without making a sound is done.
In the same way, being able to read written material quickly and understand the feeling contained in it is rapid reading.
For reading comprehension, oral reading is considered suitable at the primary and basic levels, while at the secondary and higher levels the use of silent reading and rapid reading is found to be much greater.
The present article will be of help to teachers and students connected with language teaching, and also to curriculum developers and textbook writers.
british_english:
The art of reading is the process of taking in the ideas made manifest by written symbols.
Reading comprehension is the reading and understanding of the statement and the ideas of written material.
It brings about the development of a capacity to take in a great deal of material in a short space of time.
The present study centres upon the introduction, aims, need and significance of the teaching of reading comprehension, together with the kinds of reading.
In this, a qualitative design has been adopted, material has been gathered by the library method, and exposition and analysis have been undertaken.
Reading comprehension is likewise held to be important for enabling learners to do well in the capacity to read the subject matter at a quick, a middling and a slow pace as need dictates, to grasp the ideas and the gist, to expound and analyse, and to make notes and answer questions.
Reading comprehension may be considered by distinguishing it into oral reading, silent reading and rapid reading.
If the reading aloud of the subject matter so that another person or a group may hear it is oral reading, then in silent reading the business of reading inwardly to oneself without uttering a sound is carried on.
In like manner, to be able to read written material swiftly and to understand the sentiment within it is rapid reading.
For reading comprehension, oral reading is reckoned suitable at the primary and basic levels, whereas at the secondary and higher levels the employment of silent reading and rapid reading is found to be far more extensive.
The present article will afford assistance to teachers and pupils associated with language teaching, as well as to curriculum framers and textbook authors.
